title: Dyna-Style Safety Augmented Reinforcement Learning: Staying Safe in the Face of Uncertainty
claim: A closed loop of model learning, uncertainty-aware filter learning, and safe data collection lets safe regions expand and conservatism shrink over iterations.
layout: 3 boxed stages in a cycle, clockwise arrows labeled with data, central mascot
description: A cyclic diagram of three boxed stages connected by labeled arrows. On the left, "Model Learning" shows a 2-D state-space sketch: a red hatched failure-state region contains a green hatched safe-state region. Inside that sits a pink blob outlined in cyan, the region where the model is certain and safe, filled with dense black environment-data dots. A legend sits below. An arrow labeled "Synthetic Data" leads to the top-right box, "Safety Filter Learning". That box shows a small scatter of green and red points separated by a cyan line, with the action space labeled A. A downward arrow labeled "Safety Filter" leads to the bottom-right box, "Safe Control Learning and Data Collection". That box shows a Walker-style robot between red hatched constraint bars. An arrow labeled "Environment Data" returns to the left box. A cartoon dinosaur in a helmet riding a bike with training wheels sits in the center and signals safe learning.
caption: Dyna-SAuR mechanism. An uncertainty-aware dynamics model is used to train a safety filter that avoids both failures and uncertain regions of the model. The filter is leveraged to safely learn a control policy in the environment. The collected interaction data is used to improve the dynamics model, which expands the certain area and reduces filter conservatism in the next iteration.
abstract: Safety is a key problem in reinforcement learning, especially during exploration. While safety filters are promising to address this issue, they are ill-suited for high- dimensional systems with unknown dynamics. We propose Dyna-style Safety Augmented Reinforcement Learning (Dyna-SAuR), a novel algorithm that learns a control policy as well as a safety filter requiring minimal domain knowledge by leveraging a learned uncertainty-aware dynamics model. A novel filter learning formulation requires the filter to avoid failures and areas of high model uncertainty. As joint deployment of the control policy and filter allows to safely collect data and improve the dynamics model, certain areas grow and filter conservatism decreases over time. Dyna-SAuR reduces failures compared to established safe RL baselines by two orders of magnitude on goal-reaching CartPole and MuJoCo Walker.
